subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Marshmallow Test and Financial Patience
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Marshmallow Test and Financial Patience.

hook.text: Kids who waited 15 minutes for two marshmallows had better SAT scores and finances decades later.

buildup.text: Mischel's marshmallow test measured delay of gratification: resisting a small reward for a bigger one.

discovery.text: Delayed gratification is the core skill behind saving, investing, and long-term planning.

twist.text: But follow-ups showed environment matters more than character. Kids from unstable homes ate early because waiting.

climax.text: Financial patience isn't willpower. It requires trust that the future reward will arrive. Stability enables patience.

punchline.text: Patience isn't a trait. It's a luxury of trust.

quiz.question: What did follow-up studies to the marshmallow test reveal?
options: Environment and trust matter more than pure willpower
All children became equally patient as adults
